title: Private: KMS key_id case drift causes RBAC mapping failure and audit suppression (urgent patch + rollback plan)
creator: Priya Nair
description: Customer escalation from two on-prem Private customers: when using customer-managed KMS for envelope wrapping, audit logs and RBAC role resolution intermittently failed. Symptoms: requests authenticated successfully but mapped roles were missing and audit pipeline dropped events because key metadata did not match expected canonical key identifier. Impacted only Private control-plane integrations where the KMS client returned a key identifier with differing capitalization (example: 'KeyId: projects/project/locations/global/keyRings/ring/cryptoKeys/CustomerKey' vs expected lowercase 'keyr.../customerkey'). This caused downstream RBAC policy lookup to treat keys as unknown, producing missing role assignments and a filter in the audit ingestion that suppressed events for unknown key ids.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy Private control plane with customer KMS configured and set envelope wrapping to use customerKey.
2) Trigger token rewrap flow from on-prem worker to control plane (observed in customer environment during key rotation).
3) Observe control plane log: KMS response header 'KeyId' present but cased differently than the canonical mapping used by RBAC cache (case-sensitive map lookup).
4) Inspect audit pipeline: event filter rules drop entries for key ids not in canonical form, resulting in missing audit events for a subset of requests.
root_cause: A case-sensitivity assumption in control-plane KMS client integration: the KMS response returned a key identifier with mixed/camel case. The RBAC key->tenant mapping used a case-sensitive hash map, and the audit ingestion rules only matched the canonical lowercased key id. A missing normalization step during the KMS unwrap/rewrap path caused two failure modes: 1) RBAC role lookup returned empty because key id string did not match mapping; 2) audit pipeline filters suppressed events for unknown key identifiers. This was exposed during customer-driven key rotations and intermittent TTL-based KMS client caching behavior which returned the key id variant.
mitigation: Immediate mitigation applied: 1) Roll forward a control-plane feature flag 'kms_keyid_normalize' to true for affected customers to normalize key ids to lowercase at ingest time. 2) Re-enable permissive audit path: temporarily bypass audit filtering for unknown key ids and emit debug audit entries to object storage for retention until canonicalization completes. 3) Notified affected customers and recommended skipping rotation if possible until patch deploy completes.
plan: Short-term: ship hotfix that normalizes KMS key_id at the KMS client boundary and updates RBAC cache population to use normalized keys. Also patch audit ingestion to accept canonicalized and raw forms for 72 hours and write both to the audit store. Long-term: add end-to-end validation tests in CI for KMS response normalization, add metrics and alerts for KMS key variance, and add documentation for acceptable key identifier formats for Private deployments.
pr_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/8765 -- WIP: normalize KMS key id at unwrap path
https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-ingest/pull/430 -- Accept both canonical and raw key id; preserve raw for debug
deploy_plan: 1) QA hotfix branch with customer-mirroring infra in staging. 2) Canary deploy to single affected Private customer region with audit debug enabled. 3) Monitor RBAC resolution metrics and audit ingestion success for 24h. 4) If stable, rollout to remaining affected customers and then to general Private fleet. 5) Post-deploy: run audit replay job to recover dropped events from raw debug store.
